Gain perturbation applies a scaling factor to visual hand movement based on real hand motion: Visual hand velocity = (1 + gain) * real hand velocity (0% = visual hand moves like the real hand; -100% = visual hand does not move; 100% = visual hand moves twice as fast). Gain is applied relative to the origin defined in 'origin' tab -> Visual hand distance from origin = (1 + gain) * real hand distance from origin. Gain is applied indepdendently to each axis (e.g. applying a -50% gain in Y only slows down vertical movement only).

Gain values are defined per hand/per axis (gain applies symmetrically - positive gain increases the magnitude of movement away from the origin / negative gain compresses it - regardless of the specific direction along axis  - e.g. right vs left)
